title: The Moon and its shapes
examples: Why does the moon look different every night?
Does the moon make its own light?

explain.say: The moon changes its shape over time.
Now look! Here it is in 3D: the phases of the Moon. Can you see the sunlight and the earth? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.
The full moon is when the moon looks its brightest.
A half moon means exactly half of the moon is lit.
A crescent moon is a little curved sliver of light.
The moon does not make its own light to shine.
When we see the moon, we see sunlight bouncing off it.

faq.q: Why does the moon change shape?
faq.a: The moon orbits the Earth, and we only see the part lit by the Sun. As it moves, we see different amounts of light.
asks: Why does the moon look different every night?
What causes the moon's changing shape?

faq.q: Does the moon make its own light?
faq.a: No, the moon only reflects the light that comes from the Sun. It acts like a giant mirror in space.
asks: Is the moon bright because it glows?
Where does the moon get its light from?

faq.a: The full moon is the time when the entire face of the moon is lit up for us to see.
asks: When is the moon completely lit?
What does a full moon look like?

faq.a: A crescent moon is when only a small, curved sliver of the moon is visible. This happens when the moon is close to the Sun.
asks: What is the little curved moon shape?
When is the moon a thin curve?

faq.q: Does the moon cycle take a set amount of time?
faq.a: Yes, the moon cycle takes about one month to complete all its changes. This is how we track the phases.
asks: How long does the moon cycle last?
Is the moon cycle always the same length?

facts: The moon reflects sunlight; it does not produce its own light.
The full moon happens when the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon.
The phases change because of the changing angles between the Sun, Earth, and Moon.

quiz.say: If the Sun, Earth, and Moon are lined up, what phase is it?
quiz.why: When the Moon is between the Sun and Earth, we cannot see its lit side.

wrong.0: This is wrong because lining up means the Moon is either completely hidden or fully visible, not half.
wrong.1: This is wrong because a crescent means only a small part is lit, not that it is hidden.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the Moon must be on the opposite side of the Earth from the Sun to be fully lit.

quiz.say: What do we see when the Moon is at its brightest?
quiz.why: The full moon means the entire face we see is lit up by the Sun.

wrong.0: This is wrong because a half moon is only half lit, not completely bright.
wrong.1: This is wrong because a crescent is a small, curved sliver of light.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the new moon means the side facing us is dark.

quiz.say: If the Moon is getting bigger each night, what is this phase called?
quiz.why: Waxing means the illuminated part of the moon is increasing in size.

wrong.0: This is wrong because 'New' means the moon is not visible at all.
wrong.2: This is wrong because waning means the lit part is getting smaller.
wrong.3: This is wrong because 'Full' describes the size, not the change over time.
